page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory bandwidth, with uncached read and write speeds placing in the top 25% of tested systems. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), contribute to strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Image processing benchmarks show top-tier performance in the top 10% of its class. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 396.8 tokens per second with small 135M parameter LLM models, though performance drops to a weak rating of 2.77 tokens per second when executing text generation on large 70B parameter models.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D32lds_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-intensive workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of a high-capacity 1890 GB local NVMe SSD provides fast temporary storage, reducing dependency on external network-attached disks. This hardware balance makes the server suitable for web serving, image processing, software compilation, and moderate-sized machine learning inference tasks, while it is less optimal for memory-heavy databases or large-scale LLM deployments.
